title: DFT Frequency Bin Explorer
description: A live row of DFT bins with DC and Nyquist highlighted, recomputing every center frequency, the bin width, and the unique-bin count as N and the sampling rate change.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Frequency Analysis
DFT

educational.topic: DFT bin width and frequency resolution
learningObjectives: Calculate bin width from N and the sampling rate
Demonstrate the resolution versus bin-count tradeoff
prerequisites: A DFT turns N samples into N frequency values

controls.label: Any bin
controls.purpose: Show its exact center frequency and covered range

equations: center frequency of bin k = k * fs / N
unique bins for a real input = N/2 + 1
assumptions: N is a power of two
limitations: Shows bin geometry only; the actual response shape of a bin, including sidelobes, is covered elsewhere

keyQuestions: What happens to bin width when N doubles?
What do you give up by halving the sampling rate to improve resolution?
commonMisconceptions: That resolution can be improved by computing harder on the same capture
That all N bins carry unique information for a real input
assessmentOpportunities: Find the smallest N that resolves two tones 40 Hz apart at 16 kHz
